module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil


/-!
# Erdős Problem 355

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/355](https://www.erdosproblems.com/355)
- [DoKo25] W. van Doorn and V. Kovač, Lacunary sequences whose reciprocal sums represent all
  rationals in an interval. arXiv:2509.24971 (2025).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos355

/--
Is there a lacunary sequence $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ (so that $A=\{a_1 < \cdots\}$ and
there exists some $\lambda > 1$ such that $a_{n+1}/a_n\geq \lambda$ for all $n\geq 1$) such that
$$\left\{ \sum_{a\in A'}\frac{1}{a} : A'\subseteq A\textrm{ finite}\right\}$$
contain all rationals in some open interval?

Bleicher and Erdős conjectured the answer is no.

In fact the answer is yes, with any lacunarity constant $\lambda\in (1,2)$ (though not $\lambda=2$),
as proved by van Doorn and Kova\v{c} [DoKo25].

This was formalized in Lean by van Doorn using Aristotle.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/Woett/Lean-files/blob/main/ErdosProblem355.lean"]
theorem erdos_355 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∃ A : ℕ → ℕ, IsLacunary A ∧ ∃ u v : ℝ, u < v ∧ ∀ q : ℚ, ↑q ∈ Set.Ioo u v →
      q ∈ {∑ a ∈ A', (1 / a : ℚ) | (A' : Finset ℕ) (_ : ↑A' ⊆ Set.range A)} := by
  sorry


end Erdos355

reformulations.difference: The source uses a positive, strictly increasing integer sequence with a uniform consecutive-ratio bound at every index. Lean instead requires only eventual strict multiplicative growth through IsLacunary, allowing zero and irregular or repeated values in a finite initial segment.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An IsLacunary sequence has a strictly increasing, unbounded tail. Enumerate its positive range in increasing order. Beyond finitely many initial values this enumeration agrees with the original tail, so its consecutive ratios have a uniform lower bound greater than 1: combine the tail bound with the minimum of the finitely many exceptional ratios, each greater than 1. Sorting and removing repetitions do not change the range-based finite sums, and deleting zero does not change them either because (1 / 0 : ℚ) = 0. Thus the same interval is covered. Conversely, a positive sequence with ratios at least λ > 1 satisfies IsLacunary by choosing a strict bound between 1 and λ. The complete existential equivalence was proved as Review.source_equivalence in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without using the target theorem.
